title: Carl Bonde and Nils Lillieroot's ciphered French memorial to Louis XIV (6/16 Oct 1676) and Bonde's Swedish despatch of 24 Nov/4 Dec 1677: one number table (Riksarkivet, Diplomatica Gallica; catalogue 2317), read in part

steps.what: Volume R0003797 surveyed for catalogue row 2317. The 'bare' leaves of the lead (images 107-109) are the cipher tail of the despatch of 11/21 Nov 1675, already deciphered in the chancery gloss on images 102-106. The real unread matter: a French memorial in cipher, images 321R-326R.

Key v1 rebuilt from the gloss on image 102R (488 cipher numbers against 566 gloss letters, one letter a number) by EM alignment; v2 corrected from 107L/105L and given values 100-176 from 14 training lines of image 324L (tier F).
Control: 10 rows of image 107L transcribed and frozen, decoded once with v1, then found word for word in the gloss on image 105L. Catalogue correction: 107-109 are not unread.

First test, FAILED: 30 held-out lines of image 324 frozen and decoded once with key v2: strict 44/103 = 42.72% (S+E 88.35%), under the 65% bar the contributor had set for this test; 0 of 5,000 shuffled keys (two seeds). Key v3 was then built from the same lines, so image 324 is in-sample for v3 and gets no count.

Key v3 = v2 + tier-P values read off the image-324 test lines after the test, and 88 corrected to m; frozen 02:55:22 UTC (md5 8e1d93d1) before any other page of the memorial was transcribed. Image 324 is therefore in-sample for v3. (By the contributor's record; the stamped manifest of 02:54:07 GMT holds a file byte-identical to key v3, before any stamp that holds a held-out page.)
Six pages (f.307v-311r) transcribed and each frozen before one decode with v3 unchanged: strict 358/486 = 73.66% as filed in #453; 346/486 = 71.19% after the correction in overrides.tsv.
Opening found on f.306r (image 321R; image 322 is not the start). f.306r-307r transcribed, frozen and decoded once with v3 unchanged: strict 200/278 = 71.94%.

5,000 shuffled keys per page and pooled, French 4-gram model (Language header asserted): 0 of 5,000 on every page; all nine pages pooled, true -2.1534 against best -4.6480 (seed 20261112) and -4.5698 (seed 7).

Blind second transcription of f.307v and f.309v (b103): 860 of 863 full numerals the same; two disputes settled for the first transcription on crops, one open. Its decode with v3: 122/182 against 123/182.
French reading with supplied letters bracketed and English translation (readings/, translations/).
Prior art: see conditions.prior_solution. Trolle-Bonde D.1 (1910) not seen.

Folder rebuild (b154): every filed figure reproduced by scripts/build.py, compare_blind.py and run_controls.py; 12 units counted S in the filing read 66 as the Swedish value a-ring where French needs y; downgraded in overrides.tsv.

Key v3 extended for Swedish text: v4-v7 add values read from context in the despatches of 6/16 and 13/23 Oct 1676 and the post-hoc values of the memorial (tiers Q, T); v8 and v9 add only values read off the chancery's interlinear glosses of 1676-1677 (images 331, 334, 336, 341, 346, 395, 429, 430; tiers G, H). v9 frozen 06:08:58 UTC, md5 af29e81f (by the contributor's record: the stamp of 06:25:27 came after the decode).
Survey of images 379-557: glossing stops about Nov 1677; the bare despatches of late 1677 are the held-out pool. 489R carries cipher and no gloss.
489R transcribed (169 numbers in 17 runs), frozen 06:24:26 UTC with a doubts file, then decoded once with v9 unchanged: strict 24/30 = 80.00%.
5,000 shuffled keys, Swedish 4-gram model (Language header asserted): 0 reach the true score (true -3.1451; best -4.0151 seed 20261112, -3.9637 seed 7).
Wimarson I-III screened for this despatch: not cited. Höjer 1875, Trolle-Bonde D.1, Grauers 1926 not reached.

Truly blind second transcription (b127; nothing of b118-b120 or the key opened before its freeze at 09:35:28 UTC): 168 of 169 numbers the same; its decode with v9 23/30 = 76.67%, 0 of 5,000 shuffled keys.

Folder rebuild (b154): every filed figure reproduced; the source of each key value used in the read units counted (counts.txt): 22 of the 24 read units use at least one value read from context, not from a gloss.

Integration check (R4, AI agent): own decoder written from key.tsv alone; all 284 cipher lines of the nine held-out memorial pages and of 489R decode identically to the contributor's decryptions. About 400 groups compared with the Riksarkivet images (489R all 17 runs; f.307r lines 1-6 and 18-22; f.309v lines 4-12): 0 disagreements. Strict counts recomputed from units.tsv: 546/764 and 24/30.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the Swedish chancery's interlinear decipherments of Bonde's despatches in the same volume (the memorial's key v3 from image 102R of 11/21 Nov 1675; the 1677 despatch's key v9 from further glosses of 1676-1677), finished with values read from context (52 of v3's 119 letter rows from image 324 of the memorial itself; 58 of the 149 numbers in the read units of 489R), frozen, and applied unchanged to pages that carry no gloss. Context-derived values are marked on the page.
outcome.fraction_read_source: units.tsv and counts.txt of the two folders (scripts/build.py): 546 of 764 word units of the nine held-out memorial pages (key v3) and 24 of 30 of the 489R despatch (key v9) are spelt by frozen letter values; codes, cuts, unvalued, weak and emended units never count. 570 of 794 together (71.8%). Unit = a word of the plaintext.

texts.label: Bonde and Lillieroot to Louis XIV, memorial, [Paris, 6/16 Oct 1676], f.306r-311r
texts.summary: The Swedish envoys thank Louis XIV for declaring war on Denmark under the guarantee of the Northern treaties and report Charles XI's victory at Halmstad, then press him: turn his arms on Denmark and send troops and ships under the treaty; as Pomponne says that cannot be done, ready a squadron to reach Gothenburg early in spring 1677 and join the ten ships there; the allies will make no peace until France returns its conquests and count on taking Pomerania; any French peace must restore Sweden's lost places; pay an extraordinary subsidy for stores from England and Holland for Stralsund and Gothenburg and for Pomerania; win Hamburg with free trade. Context: the Scanian War (1675-79), with Sweden's German provinces under attack, while the Nijmegen peace talks went on.

texts.label: Carl Bonde (Paris) to Charles XI, 24 Nov/4 Dec 1677, cipher on 489R
texts.summary: Bonde reports that the French court is much displeased: someone coming to Livonia, learning of Pac's opposition, means to delay and hold back the [418] (march?) until the matter with Pac is settled, in the form of a vain negotiation, which has alarmed the court. The French want nothing more than the plans, with a prompt diversion into [435] (Prussia?), carried out, and the King's Field Marshal to bring the [418] to ripeness as soon as possible so that the suspicions are dropped. Context (our inference): French-backed plans of late 1677 for a Swedish diversion from Livonia, with the passage of Lithuanian troops, which the despatch of 3/13 Nov 1677 also concerns.
